sources.text: A command deadline bounds one request. The worker lease bounds ownership across requests. A successful command does not renew the lease.
Renewal is performed by the lease heartbeat. After lease expiry the worker must stop accepting commands, even when the last command completed successfully.
The routing article explains destination selection. The retry article explains recovery after transient failure. Both use the same transport trace.
Sharing a transport trace does not make routing and retry interchangeable. Preserve retry limits when consolidating the operational guide.
The current retention policy is fourteen days. This revision supersedes the former thirty-day policy; thirty days is historical, not current guidance.
Exports created before the policy revision are retained under their original legal hold. The new fourteen-day limit does not release a legal hold.
The scanner's owner has not been recorded. The repair queue is explicitly unassigned. These are different states; absence of a scanner owner is not evidence that nobody owns it.
Mina will investigate the missing scanner roster entry. Investigation responsibility does not appoint Mina as the scanner owner.
An admitted article is eligible for drafting. Publication still requires citation validation. Admission alone never makes an article searchable.
A failed citation check parks the draft for review. Recovery retries validation rather than marking the failed article published.
Removing a source invalidates its citations. A later rebuild must not resurrect removed evidence from a cached article.
Protected human prose stays editable only by its owner. Protection does not preserve the validity of a citation to a removed source.
The archive snapshot records what was available on January 31. It is not an active catalog and may include products withdrawn since that date.
Only the current catalog authorizes new orders. Historical snapshot entries remain useful for audit, not for order eligibility.
The north region has a reserved quota of forty units. Unused north capacity cannot be transferred automatically to south.
An incident commander may approve a temporary cross-region allocation. Such approval is incident-scoped and does not change the permanent regional quotas.
Calibration corrected the sensor offset from plus four degrees to plus one degree. Earlier readings must retain the old offset when reconstructed.
No observations were captured during the battery outage. Interpolation is an estimate and must not be presented as a measured temperature.
Rotating a signing key prevents issuance under the retired key. Existing sessions remain valid until their token expiry unless separately revoked.
For a compromised key, incident response requires explicit session revocation. Routine key rotation alone is not equivalent to revoking sessions.
The search cache refreshes every hour. A cache hit can be stale and cannot authorize an account suspension.
Suspension decisions read the authoritative account record at decision time. A cached search preview is navigation evidence only.
Settlement requests carry an idempotency key. A timeout does not establish that settlement failed; query the ledger before issuing a new key.
Retries reuse the original key while the outcome is unknown. A different key can create a second settlement and requires explicit reconciliation.
Harbor has completed functional tests. Production rollout is blocked until the capacity review approves peak-load headroom.
Ravi owns Harbor delivery. Lena reviews capacity. A pending Lena review is not ownership transfer and functional completion is not launch approval.
Cedar's incident mitigation was deployed to the affected shard. The incident is resolved, but the general rollout remains paused for compatibility testing.
Omar owns compatibility testing. The incident commander Sia closed the incident; closure does not approve the general rollout.
Juniper delivery belongs to Chen. Bea is the security reviewer and has not accepted delivery ownership.
The security review is scheduled, not completed. Implementation may continue in the isolated test environment while release approval remains pending.
Maple is blocked on the parser migration. Birch uses the same library but is not blocked because it uses the legacy interface.
Dara owns the parser migration. Maple and Birch retain separate release decisions; shared dependency does not imply shared status.
Willow's target moved from April 3 to April 17. April 17 is a planning target, not a committed shipment date.
The vendor has not confirmed hardware arrival. The schedule remains contingent on that arrival; the earlier April 3 target is obsolete.
Aspen's accountable owner is unknown in the handoff record. Niko will locate the record but is not assigned accountable ownership.
The migration checklist is explicitly unassigned. Owner discovery and checklist assignment are separate unresolved tasks.
Orchid is available in east. West launch is blocked by residency approval, not by east availability or functional readiness.
Iman owns west launch. Tao can review residency evidence but cannot grant the required legal approval.
Saffron's prototype passed the demo review. Accessibility testing has not started, so demo success is not a readiness signoff.
Eli owns the prototype. Noor is arranging accessibility testers; arranging testers does not make Noor the delivery owner.
Moss rolled back the production optimizer after latency increased. The isolated research experiment remains active and has not been cancelled.
Pia owns rollback verification. Any new production attempt requires fresh latency evidence and separate approval.
Flint has budget approval for a trial batch only. Approval does not cover full-volume procurement.
Trial delivery is expected in May but the supplier has not committed a date. Full procurement remains blocked on certification.
Linden copied all records to the destination. Validation is incomplete; source deletion is prohibited until audit reconciliation passes.
Uma leads migration delivery. Vic independently reviews reconciliation. A completed copy is not a completed migration.
Quartz credential renewal is complete. Iris still uses the retired credential and is blocked from the next release until its own renewal completes.
Wen coordinates both initiatives but only owns Quartz. Iris ownership is not recorded; do not infer it from coordination.
